name: Log jail

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

placement.position_note: PLACED 2026-08-11. THE CORNER IS DOCUMENTED AND THE COORDINATE IS DERIVED, so the tag follows the weaker half. Andreas puts the log jail on 'the northwest corner of the court-house square'. The public square is the block bounded by Randolph Street on the north, Washington Street on the south, Clark Street on the east and LaSalle Street on the west - the block this project's own ground control identifies as such in data/traces/gcp/wright_1834_gcps.json, where LaSalle and Randolph is labelled 'NW corner of the Public Square block' and Clark and Washington 'SE corner of the Public Square block'. Its four inside corners were computed for this parcel from modern OpenStreetMap intersection centres fetched 2026-08-11, offset 12.2 m into the block on each axis, half of an 80 ft street per Hathaway 1834: NW 447538.25 / 4637130.78, NE 447639.27 / 4637130.25, SW 447541.20 / 4637018.49, SE 447639.80 / 4637018.05, which makes the block about 101 x 112 m. The jail's own north-west corner is set on the square's north-west corner, so the footprint origin - which is the building's south-west corner - sits its own depth south of it. THIS IS A CORNER OF A BLOCK, NOT A LOT, so it is a weaker statement than the corner-lot placements elsewhere in this dataset: nothing says how far into the block the building stood, whether it was set back from either street line, or which way it faced. WORKING UNCERTAINTY ABOUT 20 M from the georeference (data/datum.json: 17.5 m RMS on Wright 1834, 3.7 per cent paper stretch), plus an unquantified setback into the block. Facade bearing 0, due north onto Randolph, CONVENTION RATHER THAN EVIDENCE - a jail at the north-west corner could as reasonably have faced west onto LaSalle or inward onto the square, and nothing attests it. The square itself in 1835 was otherwise an open, unimproved prairie block, fenced or not; no fence, path or improvement of the block is modelled. RECONCILED WITH THE COMMITTED PLAT 2026-08-28 (T-0246), AND THE CLAIM DID NOT MOVE - ONLY THE LINE IT WAS DERIVED AGAINST. The method above found the square's north-west corner by taking modern OpenStreetMap intersection centres, fetched 2026-08-11, and stepping 12.2 m into the block on each axis. That is not this project's own Randolph Street: the committed centreline in data/streets/1835.json, offset by half the committed 80 ft corridor, is what tools/generate_plat_lots.py builds every platted block edge from, and it is the line every derived layer in this scene reads. Measured against it with tools/measure_corridor_intrusion.py, this footprint's north wall stood 3.48 m OUT PAST blk_randolph_lasalle's Randolph frontage line, in the platted roadway, with its centroid inside the corridor - deeper than any of the four Lake Street records T-0196 looked at - and tools/generate_frontage_works.py refused two steps of Randolph's plank walk, 0.0 to 10.4 m along that face, naming this building in the refusal. THE REPAIR IS THIS RECORD'S OWN METHOD RUN AGAINST THIS PROJECT'S OWN LINE: the footprint is translated 4.981 m along the face's inward normal - dE -0.040 m, dN -4.981 m in local ENU, so UTM E 447538.25 N 4637126.21 becomes E 447538.21 N 4637121.23 - which leaves its north wall 1.50 m back from the committed frontage line. THE SQUARE IS NOT SUBDIVIDED, so there is no lot line to stand off: 1.50 m is plat_occupancy.LOT_MARGIN_M, the plat module's own margin off a boundary, and it is the same figure the reconciled South Water and Lake records took off their lot lines (T-0127, T-0198, T-0199). NOTHING ALONG THE STREET MOVED: the along-face position, the block, the corner and the side are untouched, and so is the confidence grade - re-deriving a coordinate from better geometry is not new evidence, and Andreas's 'northwest corner of the court-house square' is what it always was. WHAT THIS DOES NOT REPAIR: the 20 m working uncertainty stated above is unchanged and dwarfs this 4.98 m, so the move is a reconciliation between two of this project's own lines and not a claim to have located the jail better. The facade bearing stays 0 while this face runs at 0.46 degrees, which leaves the front wall between 1.50 and 1.55 m back across its width; that skew is not corrected here, because rotating a record is a second claim and this one is a repair. V4 ENCLOSURE/ACCESS RECONSTRUCTION 2026-10-30: the earlier exact northing was a chosen setback derived from the public-square street line, not an attested building coordinate. Andreas attests the northwest part of the square, not the exact setback. Move only 1.30 m south within the stated roughly20 m working uncertainty, retaining easting, bearing, core fabric, footprint, parcel and every committed street input. This finite R placement allows the existing1.80 m native doorway approach plus0.25 m to the continuous palisade axis atN-269.25 (0.16 m beyond a180 mm backing post), rather than preserving an invented centre gap that is absent from the1902 drawing. The exact1.30 m is an access/layout convention, not survey evidence or a measured pictorial distance. The1836-captioned plate does not establish the July1835 arrangement; continuity remains R. The earlier placement and plat-reconciliation history above is retained as history, not a claim that the later R setback is derived.

    why
  
    
  
      
    Was it inside the town's fire limit?
    Inside the limit — hay could not lawfully be stacked here.
    Section 22 of the by-laws the Trustees passed on
      5 August 1835 made it unlawful to stack hay inside a boundary they walked street
      by street — 198.9 acres
      of it — under twenty-five dollars a stack. It is the town's own statement of where
      it was built up closely enough to burn, five weeks after this scene.
    commencing on Washington street, at the United States Reservation, and running thence West to the intersection of Canal Street, thence North to the intersection of Kinzie Street, thence East to the intersection of Wolcott street, thence to Illinois Street, and thence to Lake Michigan
    The Chicago Democrat, 19 August 1835, page 1 —
      the limit is derived from committed street lines, never drawn in the scene.
  
      
    Was it here?
    
      
    recorded standing
    1833-10-01 → 1835-12-31inferred
    sources: Andreas, A. T. History of Chicago: From the…Andreas: 'During the fall of 1833, the citizens felt that something more metropolitan was required than the estray pen', and a log jail was built (the research notes on structures south section 7, from Andreas I scan pp. 367 and 1243). A SEASON IS THE WHOLE OF THE DATING. 1833-10-01 is the middle of a northern-Illinois autumn and is a bound rather than a date; the building is standing well before the scene date on any reading of 'fall'. THE END IS A HOUSEKEEPING BOUND, NOT A DEMOLITION DATE - nothing reached says when this jail came down or was replaced, and 1835-12-31 is the ordinary continuity cut at the scene year this dataset uses where a fate is unattested.
    why
  
    
  
      
    Was it this shape?
    
      
    footprint
    reconstructed
    INVENTED. NO SOURCE REACHED GIVES THIS BUILDING A DIMENSION, a plan, or a number of cells. 6.096 x 4.572 m is 20 x 15 ft, recorded converted with the original figures stated per the datum json's data units rule. The only constraint the evidence offers is relative and it runs in both directions: the jail was built because something more metropolitan was required than the estray pen, so it is a more substantial thing than a stock pound; and it was itself superseded within a few years, so it was small. A 20 x 15 ft log box is a two-cell lock-up and is the smallest thing that answers both. Nothing else about the shape is a finding: the plain rectangle, the proportion and the scale are all this record's.

        Attributes and evidence
        
    built
    1833attested
    sources: Andreas, A. T. History of Chicago: From the…Andreas: the log jail was built in the fall of 1833.
    why
  
    construction
    logattested
    sources: Andreas, A. T. History of Chicago: From the…The building is named a LOG jail in the only description this project has of it, which makes the material the single best-attested thing about it. THE PLATE NOW SETTLES THE SECOND HALF OF IT: the engraving of the first Cook County jail in the owner's 2026-08-18 brief (the source files for owner brief of 2026-08-18, image 1) draws squared timber laid horizontally — 'a low log jail — squared timber, near-flat roof' — which is hewn log in courses with notched corners, exactly what this archetype builds for this value (the logwork generator). Until 2026-08-21 this note said hewn-versus-round was unattested and the archetype's hewn wall was a convention standing where evidence should be; the plate is that evidence, at a modern reconstruction, for the FABRIC and not for any dimension. Whether the walls were single or doubled, and whether they were lined inside, nothing reached says. The plate is a PICTORIAL (a modern reconstruction) held here as the brief's written record rather than a committed binary — the images were supplied in-session and other work owns identifying them against the Andreas plate numbering and creating the source record — so it is cited by path, the way this dataset's other brief-driven attributes are (Green Tree Tavern chimneys, image 6). The value's own grade is unchanged: 'log' was attested by Andreas before the plate and still is.
    why
  
    function
    jailattested
    sources: Andreas, A. T. History of Chicago: From the…Purpose-built for confinement, and it is the building that ended the practice recorded on the Estray pen record - prisoners held in the stock pound for want of anywhere else. Cook County was organised in 1831 and the county's business was conducted in rented rooms; this is the first purpose-built county structure of any kind and it precedes the court-house on the same block by about two years.
    why
  
    door
    maninferred
    Not attested. `door` in this archetype names what has to get through the opening rather than whether there was one. A jail takes a person through in hand and nothing else - no horse, no wagon - so the man-door class is the reading, and it is the only one whose 1.88 m clear height fits under this wall. Where the door stood, what it was made of, and whether it was barred or grated is not attested and is the archetype's default.
    why
  
    roof pitch deg
    12inferred
    12 DEGREES, THE PLATE'S NEAR-FLAT ROOF INSTEAD OF THIS ARCHETYPE'S DEFAULT. Superseded 2026-08-21. The value was 32.0 — the outbuilding archetype's own gable default, kept deliberately on 2026-08-11 because nothing attested a pitch and a fresh guess would have looked like a finding. The engraving of the first cook county jail in the owner's 2026-08-18 brief (the source files for owner brief of 2026-08-18, image 1) is that evidence, and it is about this particular building: 'a low log jail — squared timber, near-flat roof'. A convention loses to a picture of the thing itself, so the pitch comes down. 12 degrees is the reading of 'near-flat' at this building's scale — 0.49 m of rise over the 2.29 m half-span, a cap on a box rather than a cabin's gable, and the whole building 0.94 m lower to its ridge than it stood yesterday. NOT LOWER THAN THAT, and the floor is the covering: this archetype roofs an outbuilding in boards laid down the slope rather than shingles (the outbuilding generator _roof plane), and a lapped board roof weighted or nailed down is the frontier form that goes near-flat where a riven-shake field cannot — the archetype's own note puts shakes at about 18 degrees minimum. WHAT IS INFERRED IS THAT THE PITCH IS LOW, NOT THAT IT IS 12: no plate can be measured to a degree, and a pictorial (a modern reconstruction) may drive form and never a dimension of the ground.
    why
  
    roof type
    gableinferred
    GABLE IS KEPT, AND THE PLATE IS WHY THE PITCH MOVED RATHER THAN THE FORM. The engraving of the first cook county jail in the owner's 2026-08-18 brief (the source files for owner brief of 2026-08-18, image 1) draws a near-flat roof. That is a statement about PITCH — this record's roof pitch (deg) now carries it — and it is not a statement about whether the roof fell one way or two: the brief holds the plate as a written description, and 'near-flat' distinguishes neither. So the form stays what it was reasoned to on 2026-08-11, and the reasoning is unchanged: gable is the near-universal roof form for log construction of this type, period and region, and it is what this project's other log buildings carry. The archetype would default a building this shallow to a shed roof, which is a covering appropriate to a lean-to; a purpose-built county jail is stated as gabled rather than left to that default. Typological derivation, not a measurement — and a single-slope reading of the same plate would be a legitimate rival that nothing this project holds can settle.
    why
  
    wall height (m)
    2.66inferred
    No figure is attested. 2.66 m is about 8 ft 9 in to the plate: a man's standing height with a header over the door and a course or two above it, which is what a lock-up needs and no more. It is also, to the centimetre, what this archetype's own size-aware default computes for a 20 x 15 ft footprint, and it is kept deliberately. THE PLATE CORROBORATES THE DIRECTION AND DOES NOT REPLACE THE NUMBER: the engraving of the first Cook County jail in the owner's 2026-08-18 brief (the source files for owner brief of 2026-08-18, image 1) draws a low, squat building, which is what a 2.66 m wall under a near-flat roof already is, and moving the figure to match a picture that carries no scale would be inventing a measurement out of an impression. What is inferred is that the height falls in this range, not that it is exactly 2.66 m. The squatness the plate shows is carried by roof pitch (deg), which is the attribute the plate can actually speak to.

record:
The record's own account
    
      in the record's own words
      CURRENT COMPOUND INCREMENT: John Beach's separate keeper house, a continuous pointed palisade front and a low braced hung gate are represented as one source-informed continuity reconstruction. Gale1902 p51 places the house partly within the enclosure facing Randolph during an1835-framed recollection; the accompanying plate explicitly says1836. Neither source supplies a metric site plan or proves this exact July1835 state. The domestic house supersedes the older one-roof/open-square assertion. The original log-cell geometry and shallow12degree roof remain unchanged, with a1.30m southward reconstructed access setback explicitly declared in position.note. The Gale comparison still differs in exposed rear-core roof and compound proportions; Andreas shows a conflicting shallow cap and different house elevation. Other work stays open and no picture match or geographic camera is claimed. The verified1902 US publication supplies public-domain artwork; the separately catalogued UCR copy retains its own credit and copy-specific hold.

 DATED HISTORICAL SOURCE AND MODEL RATIONALES FOLLOW, preserved from the preceding record; older statements of no new placement or a sole roof are superseded by the current paragraph and phase change note.

 CURRENT IMAGE EVIDENCE: The exact detailed jail drawing is verified in Edwin O. Gale’s 1902 book, illustrated by W. E. S. Trowbridge. Its actual title and copyright pages establish a public-domain publication; the earlier artwork-level hold below is superseded. The separate UCR copy is catalogued Date Created and/or Issued 19 September 1930, which still does not establish publication in 1930 or an item-specific reuse licence. Its required credit is Keystone-Mast Collection, UCR/California Museum of Photography, University of California at Riverside. Use the independently verified 1902 plate as the artwork source. The caption describes 1836, and the jail core is mostly concealed by its palisade; exact July 1835 form and component continuity remain unresolved. This correction derives no new geometry or asset from the UCR copy and changes no building form.

HISTORICAL MODEL RATIONALE AND DATED SOURCE REASSESSMENTS FOLLOW.

A DOCUMENTED BUILDING WITH ONE DOCUMENTED ATTRIBUTE. What is attested is that it was a jail, that it was of logs, that it went up in the fall of 1833, and that it stood at the north-west corner of the court-house square. Everything else in this record - every dimension, the roof, the wall height, the door, the bearing - is inference or invention, and the confidence view will show it as such. THE RECORD IS WORTH HAVING ANYWAY, and this is the clearest case in the parcel for the working policy behind it: on 1835-07-01 the public square carried the jail and the roofless estray pen; the brick courthouse was not erected until the fall of 1835. The earlier three-building conjecture is superseded by this record’s phase change note and the actual Andreas page176. ARCHETYPE CHOICE: outbuilding rather than log dwelling, and the difference is not cosmetic. log dwelling reads a storey count, a loft, a chimney count and a sign, and builds a dwelling's openings; outbuilding builds a plain box with one door sized by what has to get through it, and refuses a storey count outright. A jail is the second of those. The archetype's own family list - stable, shed, barn, smokehouse, privy, crib, woodshed - does not name a jail, and that is a gap in the vocabulary rather than a reason to build the wrong thing. WHAT THE PLATE ADDED, 2026-08-21 (the owner asking that the jail 'should be made more accurate' to its engraving): a pictorial (a modern reconstruction) of this building, written up as image 1 of the 2026-08-18 brief, which the record did not have when it was placed. It reached two attributes and no others. The roof came down from the archetype's 32-degree gable default to 12 degrees, because the plate draws a near-flat roof and a convention loses to a picture of the thing itself; the construction note stopped calling hewn-versus-round unattested, because the plate draws squared timber laid horizontally. It reached NEITHER dimension nor coordinate, and it may not: a pictorial (a modern reconstruction) drives form, materials and massing as inferred and never a footprint outline or a position. So the footprint is still invented and still says so. WHAT WOULD UPGRADE THIS RECORD, in order of value: any county order or contract for the jail's construction, which is the kind of document that carries a dimension, a cost or a specification for the logs; Andreas vol. 1 at page-image level around scan pp. 367 and 1243, which is where the prose transcribed into this project's dossier sits; and the Cook County Sheriff's own published jail history, cited in the dossier and not yet held as a source record here.

1902 PUBLICATION FOUND — other work, LATER SAME-DAY SUPERSESSION (2026-10-23). The exact detailed jail artwork has now been actually read in Edwin O. Gale’s 1902Reminiscences of Early Chicago and Vicinity, plate facing printed p53, source Cook County’s First Jail as it was in 1836 (published 1902). Actual title credits ILLUSTRATED BY W.E.S.TROWBRIDGE and Fleming H. Revell Company, the New file York/Toronto, MCMII; actual copyright page states 1902 and October. The independently published 1902artwork is public domain by age and unblocks project picture work from that plate. It supersedes the earlier artwork-level hold, without assuming publication from UCR’s 1930 combined date or clearing later copy-specific additions. The UCR catalogue remains check required/text only with its required credit retained. No school/Tremont permission is being extended to the jail.

NARRATIVE AND SCENE DATE REMAIN BOUNDED. Gale p25 dates arrival to 25 May 1835; p43 starts the early-morning town stroll; p51 says a small log jail is concealed by a high plank palisade and John Beach occupies a house partly in that enclosure facing Randolph. The courthouse is “just started.” Pages 52–55 continue the stroll and give no jail alteration sequence. This is a 1902 recollection framed in 1835, while the actual plate explicitly says 1836. It supports the jail/keeper-house distinction but does not measure the core or prove every pictured detail existed by 1 July 1835. The independent Andreas hip-roof contrast and separate-oaken-cell question remain. No form, dimensions, source linkage from a form attribute, date, confidence, placement or recipe changes here; earlier numeric geometry proposals remain unapplied pending actual model review. Other work stays open.

INDEPENDENT PUBLIC-DOMAIN CONTRAST. The actual Andreas’s 1884 History of Chicago vol.1 pages 175–177 were read. Page 175 distinguishes the first 1833 log jail from a later, separate oaken cell without dating the addition. Page 176 dates the first brick courthouse to FALL 1835, after the target 1 July scene. The plate on page 177, Copyright secured by A.T.Andreas 1884, shows a low house/stockade and a rear log block under a shallow hip/pyramidal cap; the same artwork is explicitly captioned FIRST COURT HOUSE AND JAIL in Andreas’s 1884 History of Cook County page 353. This confirms the jail ensemble, but not which pictured cell is the original 1833 core, its July 1835 appearance or an absolute eave/pitch. It conflicts with the taller gable in the rights-held detailed drawing. The existing model remains a provisional proxy; no roof, height, opening, date, placement or confidence value is altered by this metadata correction. Other work remains open.

    why
  
    
  
      
    Was it inside the town's fire limit?
    Inside the limit — hay could not lawfully be stacked here.
    Section 22 of the by-laws the Trustees passed on
      5 August 1835 made it unlawful to stack hay inside a boundary they walked street
      by street — 198.9 acres
      of it — under twenty-five dollars a stack. It is the town's own statement of where
      it was built up closely enough to burn, five weeks after this scene.
    commencing on Washington street, at the United States Reservation, and running thence West to the intersection of Canal Street, thence North to the intersection of Kinzie Street, thence East to the intersection of Wolcott street, thence to Illinois Street, and thence to Lake Michigan
    The Chicago Democrat, 19 August 1835, page 1 —
      the limit is derived from committed street lines, never drawn in the scene.

    dwellinginferred
    sources: Cook County’s First Jail as it was in 1836…Gale 1902 p51 places John Beach in a house beside the jail, facing Randolph, and a house is a dwelling. INFERRED and not documented, deliberately: Trowbridge's plate and Gale's recollection are a modern reconstruction pictorial and retrospective sources, and the project's evidence ladder forbids a documented value resting on a modern reconstruction alone, so the use is read off a memoir rather than attested by a period record. Who the household was beyond Beach, when the house went up and came down, where exactly it stood and every dimension of it are reconstruction, recorded on the phase and in the liberties register under “the keeper dwelling and low compound gate”.

    why
  
    siding exposure (m)
    0.152reconstructed
    INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this record wears 6 in — dealt by the siding stock generator: keyed to the phase's construction season, because buildings sided from the same season's shipments of St Joseph sawn lumber tend toward one stock, then advanced so no frame building within 60 m shares this one's. The separation is the surface variety other work reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. the liberties register “Every named frame building's siding stock is dealt, not found” owns the invention.
    why

The record's own account
    
      in the record's own words
      SOURCE-INFORMED KEEPER HOUSE, originalT-2380 incremental work. The separate house appears in Gale1902's public-domain plate captioned1836 and is described partly within the jail enclosure on p51 of the retrospective1835-framed walk. One low clapboard storey, two long-front sash followed by a door, two pictured-end ground sash, a small loft light and one stack inform the optional keeper gale 1902 layout. Metric size,25degree pitch, exact glazing, green shutter hue, whitewash, hidden framing, plan, compass, placement and July continuity remain reconstructed. The low braced gate belongs to a separate enclosure. A genuine native model pair exists for these exact resolved inputs; existing default-family models still require native parity and current registration before source adoption can pass its gates. The actual private V4 full-page compound comparison remains DIFFERS: relative compound proportions and the screened rear-core roof are unresolved, and Andreas shows a different elevation/cap. This record neither claims a complete picture match nor creates a household or population seat.
